channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Warsh and the Fed Need Clarity More Than Certainty
item.description: Kevin Warsh has rightly called into question the effectiveness of the Federal Reserve’s communications — but his arrival as chairman only seems to have made the problem worse. To put this right after the next Fed meeting this week, he’ll need to rethink his approach to explaining where things stand.
item.dc:creator: The Editors

item.title: Home Insurance: We’re Making a $3 Trillion Financial Hole Even Deeper
item.description: The first law of holes states that if you find yourself in one, stop digging. The US is in a $3 trillion home-insurance hole, but instead of putting down its shovels, it’s handing out shiny new ones that will help us dig even deeper.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gongloff

item.title: This Energy Shock Is Shredding Central Banks’ Rates Playbook
item.description: How should central banks respond to supply shocks such as oil prices jumping in the face of the US-Israel war with Iran? Policymakers have long believed these to be inherently fleeting. Hiking interest rates to counteract them, by that logic, does more harm than good; it hurts economic growth and the labor market, when simply waiting out the shock would have sufficed.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Levin

item.title: Inflation: Warsh Talked the Fed Into a Rates Trap
item.description: The need to show improvement on inflation proves too high a bar.
item.dc:creator: John Authers

item.title: Trump’s “Little War” With Iran Just Got Bigger Because of the Houthis
item.description: It is an unintended feature of President Donald Trump’s Plan B for defeating Iran — economic strangulation — that the more successful the policy becomes, the more risk the men who run the Islamic Republic are willing to accept to fight it. Judged on that metric, the American blockade and sanctions are working, but they’re also raising the stakes beyond what the US is willing to pay.
item.dc:creator: Marc Champion

item.title: Robinhood Can’t Disrupt Its Way Into the IPO Club
item.description: Robinhood Markets Inc. made it easier and cheaper for armchair investors to trade all kinds of financial markets and now it wants to open doors to initial public offerings, too. The online broker will get a chance to show what it can do with its first underwriting role, on the $3 billion listing of smart-ring maker Oura Inc.
item.dc:creator: Paul J. Davies

item.title: Portsmouth Violence: British Balaclava Mob Deserves a Hard Response
item.description: Although its leader Nigel Farage successfully campaigned for Brexit, Reform UK conforms to standard European practice in one important respect. The hard-right populist party’s continental counterparts frequently brush with the law over campaign-finance irregularities, and now Reform, too, is reeling from funding scandals that have led to a criminal inquiry by the Metropolitan Police. Farage is to be interviewed as a witness by detectives after he was allegedly filmed by undercover journalists be
item.dc:creator: Martin Ivens

item.title: Easing the Diesel Crunch Is Harder Than Keeping Planes in the Air
item.description: In times of crisis, the oil industry delivers a perennial warning: “You can’t print barrels.” While central banks can — and do — run their presses to soothe financial markets, the same option isn’t available in energy markets. And if conjuring crude is implausible, delivering diesel out of thin air is even more impossible.
item.dc:creator: Javier Blas

item.title: India Beats a Hasty Retreat From a Crucial Market Reform
item.description: After only a month of teething troubles and loud howls of protest, one of the biggest reforms in India’s capital markets in recent years risks being watered down — if not entirely jettisoned.
item.dc:creator: Andy Mukherjee

item.title: Indonesia's Green Fuel Boom Is Incinerating the Rainforest
item.description: Here’s a rare success story from Asia’s post-Hormuz energy crisis: Indonesia has managed to use biofuels to end its dependence on imported diesel. And here’s the dark side: The same policy may be exporting even more choking smoke to its neighbors.
item.dc:creator: David Fickling

item.title: Yen Rally: Bessent Doubles Down on House of the Rising Sun
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent describes himself as the top US bond salesman. He's rapidly becoming the top Japan salesman, as well. Not only does he profess to know what that country's central bank will do, he insists that anyone wanting to bet against a sustained yen rally should try him. Bravado aside, he is on to something.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Moss and Gearoid Reidy

item.title: Anthropic-Amodei Warning of AI Apocalypse Does Not Go Far Enough
item.description: Days after one of his former employees made public warnings about artificial intelligence’s threat to humanity, Anthropic’s boss Dario Amodei has responded with what looks like a solution. He’s published an essay proposing that AI labs should slow down their most cutting-edge research, to address signs that the technology might spin out of control.
item.dc:creator: Parmy Olson

item.title: China and Russia Have Sea, Space and Cyberspace Under Siege
item.description: The freedom of the global commons helped the world thrive economically and politically. China and Russia want to end it.
item.dc:creator: Hal Brands

item.title: Congress Should Follow California’s Lead on AI Laws
item.description: They called him a “doomer,” a “decel” and an “alarmist” who was too “focused on science fiction.” Turns out, Scott Wiener, the California state senator behind some of the country’s first safety regulations on artificial intelligence, was a Cassandra. All of a sudden, it appears he’s in good company.
item.dc:creator: Erika D. Smith

item.title: IPhone Duo: A Device for People Who Can’t Type
item.description: The foldable iPhone Duo, like a ride in a Cybercab, is on the list of Things I Want.
item.dc:creator: Toby Harshaw
